units.source_en: Yoichi had said that, for peace throughout the realm, the Toyotomi clan must be made to leave Osaka Castle as soon as possible. Those words clashed, if only slightly, with the spirit of “one time, one meeting,” which had been invoked several times that day.

paragraphs.source_zh: 角仓与市先前说过的话，正冷冰冰敲打着光悦的心。与市道，为了天下太平，必尽早令丰臣氏离开大坂城，这番话和今日数次被提及的“一期一会”的主旨，起了小小的冲突。

paragraphs.source_en: It was he himself who had forgotten the true meaning of ichigo ichie in the Way of Tea... Kōetsu felt that it was under his influence that Suminokura Yoichi had so rashly spoken of driving Hideyori out of Osaka. The affairs of this world were not so simple. For the sake of oneself as well as others, the highest wisdom for those born into the same age was to treat one another with sincerity.

paragraphs.source_en: I certainly do not believe that Hideyori must remain in Osaka. But conversely, to drive him out by force would be the deed of an unwise bystander. Yoichi, I beg you. You must know a way. With a generous heart, think of all the people beneath heaven: how might Hideyori be induced to leave Osaka Castle of his own accord without bringing calamity and disorder upon the realm?

units.source_zh: 与市，拜托了，你必有良方，请你以宽大之心为天下苍生念，怎样才能在不引起祸乱的情形下，让秀赖自己离开大坂城？

paragraphs.source_en: Kōetsu felt that unless he said these things aloud, his heart could never be at peace. Perhaps it was because Itakura Katsushige had just praised him so highly; and when he imagined Ieyasu even now reverently copying the words “Namu Amida Butsu” in Sunpu, Kōetsu felt that he too must inscribe “Namu Myōhō Renge Kyō” upon the earth with every step he took.

paragraphs.source_en: Yes, this was one time, one meeting. I shall bow my head and implore Yoichi to employ all his wisdom and compassion for poor Hideyori, Kōetsu thought...
